guidance.summary: Top-performing videos focus on visible everyday phenomena, nature curiosities, and mainstream hardware, maintaining retention up to 57.87%. In contrast, bottom-performing videos struggle with abstract backend software operations, niche game mechanics, and vehicle engineering specs.
do: Focus scripts on tangible visual phenomena viewers can easily visualize, such as sunset light distortion or firework chemistry.
Frame hooks around direct, active stakes or startling visual claims (e.g., PS5 Pro lying to your eyes).
Keep explainers anchored to real-world impact rather than invisible background algorithms.
avoid: Avoid covering back-end software architecture like game pre-loads, physics collision optimization, or open-source AI data processing.
Stop selecting abstract automotive spec topics like sedan fuel efficiency tricks or truck exoskeleton chassis design.
Avoid vague hooks about data streams that lack immediate personal relevance.
hook_guidance: Pair counterintuitive hooks with concrete, everyday sights (e.g., 'The sun you see is already set') rather than invisible tech processes.
Deliver the core stakes or curiosity gap within the first 5% to maintain initial viewer hold.
pacing_guidance: Target script length between 47 and 52 seconds, delivering the primary reveal early before the mid-point drop-off.
topic_guidance: Pick topics covering natural phenomena, weather mechanics, sports physics, and high-profile consumer hardware.
Skip niche game developer mechanics like asset modding, pre-load storage bloat, or haptic controller motors.
